Subject: Ownership & next steps: console telemetry / vendor SQ kickoff

Hi Marta — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap: you asked for (1) a short write-up about what telemetry our Console collects vs what appears on the docs site, (2) SOC 2 status and evidence, and (3) an initial vendor security questionnaire to kick off procurement.

- SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II in progress; we completed control testing earlier this year and expect final Type II attestation in Q3 2027. I’m attaching a one-page snapshot that summarizes scope and timeline.

- Telemetry: high-level answer: the Console collects usage events (API call metadata, route and model IDs, token counts, error traces) and standard product analytics (page views, feature events). Our docs site uses standard analytics cookies (pageviews, search) and does not collect API keys or request payloads. I’m asking Marissa to provide a concise matrix (Console vs Docs) with retention windows and opt-out controls.

- Vendor SQ: attaching our standard SQ template to start (Redwood_Security_SQ_Template.xlsx). If you can route the completed version to security@streamlinehealth.com we’ll review and return any clarifying notes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to provide the Console/docs telemetry matrix and retention table (by EOD Friday).
2) Security team to receive the SQ (we’ve attached it here). If you need a BAA for HIPAA, confirm and we’ll escalate legal.
3) If helpful, schedule a 30-min security deep-dive next week to walk your security team through the matrix.

Can you confirm preferred times next week for a call and the best contact for the SQ (security email or person)?

Thanks — looking forward to progressing this.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we push the SQ to security: 

1) When you say "usage events" in the Console, does that include request/response payloads or just metadata (e.g., method, model id, token counts)?
2) Are cookies used on the Console for user sessions? If so, are any cookies set by third-party analytics vendors on the Console domain, or only on the docs site?
3) Retention windows: can you confirm default retention for Console telemetry (events, logs, traces)? Is there a self-serve way to shorten retention for regulated customers?
4) SOC 2: happy to see the snapshot. Is there a current report we can share under NDA, and do you provide any SOC 2 cover letter for specific data processing scopes (e.g., PII, PHI)?
5) HIPAA: we may need a BAA depending on scope. Do you have a standard BAA and an estimated timeline to turn it around?
If you can answer inline I’ll pass to security and confirm who will complete the SQ. We’re aiming to finalize evaluation by mid-May.

—Marta
Head of IT Risk | Streamline Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership & next steps: console telemetry / vendor SQ kickoff
Hi Marta — looping in with answers and a couple of attachments. Inline below: 

> 1) When you say "usage events" in the Console, does that include request/response payloads or just metadata (e.g., method, model id, token counts)?

We collect metadata only by default: API call headers, route/model identifiers, token counts, latency/error metrics, and a hashed request fingerprint for dedup/diagnostics. We do not log full request/response bodies or API keys to persistent product telemetry by default. Customers can opt-in to additional debug logging (billed and time-limited) where payload sampling occurs and is stored for a defined window.
> 2) Are cookies used on the Console for user sessions? If so, are any cookies set by third-party analytics vendors on the Console domain, or only on the docs site?
Console: session cookie for user auth (HTTPOnly, Secure, SameSite=strict). We do not include third-party analytics on the Console domain by default. Docs site: uses analytics cookies (search, pageview) and includes a consent banner.
> 3) Retention windows: can you confirm default retention for Console telemetry (events, logs, traces)? Is there a self-serve way to shorten retention for regulated customers?
Default retention: events (90 days), traces/logs (365 days, aggregated metrics preserved longer). We offer configurable retention for Dedicated and Private customers; for Hosted customers we can apply contract-level retention changes (we support shorter retention for regulated customers via an SLA amendment).
> 4) SOC 2: happy to see the snapshot. Is there a current report we can share under NDA, and do you provide any SOC 2 cover letter for specific data processing scopes (e.g., PII, PHI)?
We can share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA once available — for now the attached snapshot summarizes scope. We also provide a cover letter that maps control areas to data categories on request (I’ve attached the snapshot; we’ll draft a cover letter if you need one for procurement).
> 5) HIPAA: do you have a standard BAA and timeline?
Yes — Redwood has a standard BAA. Typical turnaround after legal review is 2–3 business days for the standard form; if you require changes it can take longer. If you confirm we’ll have Legal stand up the process.
Next steps I suggest: I’ll drop the SOC snapshot into the same Drive folder and Kimberly — can you confirm the security contact to send the SQ? Once we have the contact we’ll populate the XLS and return within 48 business hours.
Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Snapshot.pdf
